analysis:
Changes in .github/workflows/release-provider.yml: (1) runs-on for resolve-env (line 135), qualify-sdk (304), stage-release (~1211) and publish-release (~1320) moved from blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404 to GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04; (2) timeout-minutes: 90 added to build-and-release (line 343). No logic, secret scoping, signing, notarization or verification steps were altered in the visible diff.

Reviewed the visible head text (lines 1-1064): source verification in resolve-env still checks out master and runs verify-source before credentials; per-environment secrets still conditioned on the resolved environment; the signing keychain is imported and then removed before any run of the built provider; notarization credentials are limited to one step; final-bytes checks (designated requirement, get-task-allow absence, CDHash, SDK, metallib symbols) are unchanged. Relevant threats are the signing/attestation chain (T-034, T-054, A-017, A-011), none weakened.

Residual considerations: moving the stage/publish jobs (which handle R2 and release-key secrets) and resolve-env to GitHub-hosted runners is a runner-trust change, but GitHub-hosted ephemeral runners are not obviously weaker than the prior third-party runner, and no evidence shows a regression. The 90-minute timeout bounds the signing job and only affects availability positively. The stage-release and publish-release bodies were outside the supplied head units (patch excerpt truncated), so I could not verify that their remaining steps are unchanged; the hunk coordinates show only the runs-on lines changed. No threat-model update is needed beyond possibly noting the runner change.
